correctness.rationale: For phases normalized a0=a3=1, Fourier orthogonality reduces the sixth-power L6 moment to 256+6(cos 3α+cos 3β)+84(cos(α−2β)+cos(2α−β))+144cos(α+β). Setting x=cos((α+β)/2) and y=cos(3(α−β)/2), independently attainable over [-1,1]², gives M6=112+288x²+12x(4x²+11)y. First minimize in y, then strictly convex φ(t)=112+288t²−48t³−132t on t=|x|∈[0,1] has unique t*=2−sqrt(111)/6, proving min 616−148sqrt(111)/3 and all phase/linear-ramp extremizers. Independently computed Fourier coefficients of P^3 at multiple non-symmetric phases and the optimizing symmetric family, agreeing with the exact identity. Binary sign enumeration gives minimum 112. Algebraic-integer obstruction for 2cos(theta*)=(12−sqrt(111))/3 forbids equality for root-of-unity phases; fourth moment 19 at cosθ=1/4 versus sixth value 385/4 proves strict tradeoff. Applies only to four consecutive circle frequencies, normalized Haar.

originality.rationale: Prior published Resultary work solves fourth moment for a four-point frequency progression and a different sharp sixth-moment maximum over arbitrary complex coefficients, not this phase-constrained sixth-moment minimum. Schmidt relates fourth moments to correlation energy, Balister et al treat asymptotic binary flatness, and Sankuru/Babu optimized fourth-moment integrated sidelobes. A historical short-polyphase exact table remains a real risk but no inspected theorem implies the sixth minimizer or algebraic phase-alphabet obstruction.

The claim does not depend on promised downstream engineering gains.
